title: Build Sherlock v1 release gate (fixture matrix, smoke suite, docs, checklist)
description:
## Problem
Sherlock has solid point fixes and fixture tests, but it does not yet have an explicit v1 release gate that proves the whole product is ready to ship.

## Goal
Create a repeatable release-readiness gate for Sherlock v1.

## Scope
- define a provider/feature fixture matrix for v1-ready paths
- add smoke coverage for the primary CLI flows (`init`, `ingest`, `report`, `rollup`, `headline`, `quota`, and `install-skill` where applicable)
- document a release checklist, known caveats, support tiers, and verification commands
- capture at least one representative sample output path for docs / sanity checking

## Why
Pre-v1 debt is not only implementation debt; it is also proof debt. v1 should have a single gate that answers "are we ready to tag?"

## Acceptance criteria
- a committed release checklist exists
- smoke commands and fixture expectations are documented and runnable
- v1 scope, caveats, and verification steps are written down in one place

title: Close provider-readiness gaps or explicitly gate previews for v1
description:
## Problem
Sherlock's registry still includes preview/stub providers that do not all meet the same verification bar. Pre-v1 needs either stronger fixture-backed readiness or an explicit narrowing of what v1 claims to support.

## Goal
Close provider-readiness gaps or deliberately gate them before v1.

## Scope
- inventory the fixture and regression-test gap for each provider in the registry
- add fixtures/tests where feasible for providers intended to be v1-ready
- keep experimental/stub providers behind explicit preview language and gating where coverage is still weak
- align README, skill docs, and CLI warnings with the actual maturity of each provider

## Why
Provider breadth is only an asset if users can tell which paths are production-grade versus exploratory.

## Acceptance criteria
- every provider in the registry has either fixture-backed coverage or explicit preview/deferred status
- README and skill docs stop over-claiming weak providers
- v1 launch scope is consistent with the implemented verification matrix

title: Surface attribution confidence and data-quality caveats
description:
## Problem
Sherlock already knows when attribution is incomplete, but the product surface still presents many results as ranked totals without consistently exposing confidence and data-quality caveats.

## Goal
Make attribution confidence and data quality first-class across JSON, Markdown, text, and TUI surfaces.

## Scope
- define exact / estimated / coarse / unavailable confidence levels for reportable metrics
- surface provider-level and session-level caveats when logs only support coarse attribution
- make missing-token-attribution findings show up as clear user-facing caveats instead of buried internals
- ensure report renderers and TUI distinguish authoritative live quota data from transcript-derived estimates

## Why
v1 should help users decide whether to trust a number, not just display the number.

## Acceptance criteria
- each report surface exposes confidence/caveat language when attribution is partial
- coarse providers no longer look equivalent to high-fidelity providers
- tests cover at least one incomplete-attribution case end-to-end

title: Decompose Sherlock core out of src/main.rs
description:
## Problem
`src/main.rs` is currently the implementation center for Sherlock: CLI dispatch, storage/schema, ingest, deterministic analysis, renderers, session selection, TUI, repo discovery, and many tests all live in one file.

## Goal
Turn `src/main.rs` into orchestration glue by extracting durable subsystems into dedicated modules.

## Scope
- extract the Dolt/store layer
- extract ingest and normalization logic
- extract deterministic analysis/report assembly
- extract renderers / TUI support code
- extract repo-discovery / time-window helpers
- preserve current CLI behavior and fixture-backed tests while improving change isolation

## Why
This is the main structural debt in the repo. It raises change risk, slows test-focused development, and makes pre-v1 feature work pile onto the same file.

## Acceptance criteria
- `src/main.rs` no longer owns the full implementation of store, ingest, analysis, rendering, and TUI internals
- the extracted module boundaries are reflected in the source tree
- existing fixture-backed report behavior remains stable

title: Define Sherlock v1 support contract and provider tier matrix
description:
## Problem
Sherlock currently advertises a broad provider set, but support quality is mixed: Claude Code and Codex are the strongest paths; Copilot CLI has coarse attribution; Cursor is explicitly experimental; Copilot VS Code is stubbed; Antigravity is shape-based and still warning-heavy.

## Goal
Define and document what Sherlock v1 actually guarantees.

## Scope
- classify each provider in `src/providers/mod.rs` as GA / preview / deferred for v1
- define the minimum bar for GA (fixture-backed ingest/report coverage, caveat language, and support expectations)
- decide how preview providers are surfaced in README, CLI warnings, and report confidence language
- make the support matrix the source of truth for docs and launch messaging

## Why
A strong v1 needs explicit trust boundaries. The product should be honest about where results are authoritative, heuristic, coarse, or incomplete.

## Acceptance criteria
- a committed support matrix exists for every provider in the registry
- README and CLI language match the chosen tiers
- v1 launch notes can point to a single provider-support contract

title: Sherlock v1 readiness program
description:
## Goal
Ship Sherlock v1 as a coherent, trustworthy system rather than a useful-but-fragmented pre-v1 CLI.

## Why now
Sherlock already has real strengths: multi-provider ingest, deterministic findings, rollup/headline/quota surfaces, and a growing fixture-backed regression base. The pre-v1 debt is now mostly about system cohesion and trust:
- core behavior is still concentrated in `src/main.rs`
- provider support tiers are implicit rather than contractual
- attribution confidence is under-expressed in the product surface
- runtime/storage ergonomics are still sharp in sandboxed environments
- release gates and launch docs are not yet codified

## Scope
This epic tracks the work needed to make v1 strong:
- define the v1 support contract and provider tier matrix
- extract the core architecture out of `src/main.rs`
- surface attribution confidence and data-quality caveats
- close provider-readiness gaps or explicitly gate previews
- land the current analysis-depth features already filed
- harden storage/runtime ergonomics for common agent environments
- create a repeatable v1 release gate with docs and smoke coverage

## Done when
Sherlock v1 has an explicit support matrix, modular core, trustworthy reporting surfaces, clear runtime ergonomics, and a release gate that can be run before tagging.

title: Feature request: One-command headline Claude usage report for modified repos
description:
## Problem
Running a full Claude Code usage analysis across many repositories is too manual and error-prone. I had to repeatedly discover modified repos, map to ~/.claude/projects encodings, ingest many JSONL files, compensate for malformed session timestamps, and then combine rollups + per-session reports to get reliable totals.

## Exact workflow used
1. Enumerated modified git repositories in ~/build and ~/class since Sunday (commit activity or dirty working tree).
2. Mapped each repo path to Claude project log directory naming convention in ~/.claude/projects (path encoded with non-alnum -> '-').
3. Counted and ingested all Claude JSONL logs newer than Sunday for each mapped repo via:
   - sherlock ingest --provider claude-code --project-root <repo> --history <jsonl>
4. Queried Sherlock/Dolt tables (sessions, turns, windows, attributions, sources) to compute:
   - per-repo total tokens and cache mix
   - active sessions since Sunday
   - top token sources and repeated findings
5. Avoided undercount from malformed started_at values (e.g., epoch-like strings ending with Z) by anchoring inclusion on windows.end_time >= Sunday and then resolving per-session totals from sherlock report output.
6. Produced ranked per-repo summary and global drivers/findings.

## Pain points
- Date filtering by sessions.started_at misses valid sessions when timestamps are malformed/inconsistent.
- No first-class command for 'analyze modified repos in date window' forces lots of custom shell + SQL glue.
- Mapping project roots to ~/.claude/projects naming is implicit and brittle.
- Rollup output can differ from expected repo-window scope unless manually constrained.

## Requested feature
Add a high-level command (example):

sherlock headline --provider claude-code --roots ~/build,~/class --modified-since sunday --window-since sunday --output markdown

Behavior:
- Discover modified repos automatically (commits + dirty state).
- Resolve provider log paths for each repo natively (no manual encoding assumptions).
- Ingest only relevant history files in the time window.
- Use robust time-window semantics that tolerate malformed session timestamps (fallback to windows/events timelines).
- Emit deterministic ranked report: per-repo totals, cache/input/output mix, top sources, dominant findings, and confidence/coverage warnings.

## Acceptance criteria
- One command reproduces the multi-repo report without external SQL/scripting.
- Date-window inclusion is correct even with malformed started_at/ended_at values.
- Output includes both active repos and modified repos with no detected usage.
- Markdown output is directly shareable with clear caveats and data-quality flags.
- Command supports JSON output for automation.

## Notes
This directly reduces repeated forensic cycles and makes Sherlock usable as a headline product workflow: quick, trustworthy, repeatable spend diagnostics across active worktrees.
close_reason: Implemented: new  subcommand + robust timestamp filter (iso_now now emits proper ISO8601; rollup filter tolerates legacy epoch-Z via session_ids_in_window fallback to windows/events).

title: Sherlock interferes with beads Dolt servers
description: Sherlock uses dolt CLI commands (dolt sql, dolt commit) which can interfere with running dolt sql-server instances that beads uses. This causes beads to have issues after running sherlock. Need to either: (1) detect running dolt servers and warn/error, (2) use SQL server protocol instead of CLI, or (3) ensure proper locking/coordination.
close_reason: Added warning system to detect running dolt servers and alert users about potential interference. Sherlock now warns when beads or other dolt-based tools are running.

title: Add session name bridge for memory
description:
Problem
Session UUIDs are hard to remember.

Requested behavior
- Introduce a human-friendly alias/name bridge for sessions
- Persist mapping (alias <-> session_id) in Sherlock store
- Allow report/tui to accept alias in place of raw session_id

Acceptance criteria
- Users can list aliases and create/update them
- report/tui resolve aliases reliably

title: Add session picker for report/tui
description:
Problem
Users must manually remember and pass --session-id.

Requested behavior
- Add interactive/default session picker for report and tui
- Show recent sessions with timestamp, project, and basic token totals
- Allow selecting latest by default and explicit selection when multiple sessions exist

Acceptance criteria
- `sherlock report` can run without --session-id by selecting latest or prompting
- `sherlock tui` supports the same selection flow
notes:
Implemented initial picker flow: report now accepts optional --session-id and defaults to latest in non-interactive mode; tui/report now use unified resolver; interactive terminals now get explicit session selection prompt when --session-id omitted and multiple sessions exist. Also removed duplicate bottom help panel from TUI.
Session picker is now project-aware: default selection prefers sessions whose project_root matches current working directory, with explicit '*' marker in interactive picker. Also added report insight when selected session has zero token totals to guide re-ingest from in-depth project logs.
Picker confusion was amplified by duplicate-session ingest artifacts; idempotent ingest fix removes repeated-record noise across reruns.

title: Fix TUI no-visible-output behavior
description:
Problem
`sherlock tui` appeared to do nothing on run.

Requested behavior
- Ensure TUI always renders visible content or clear fallback message
- Add startup diagnostics when no sessions/data exist
- Improve discoverability (e.g., initial banner/help line, explicit quit hint)

Acceptance criteria
- Running `sherlock tui` shows a visible screen state in normal terminals
- If data is missing, user gets clear guidance instead of blank/no-op behavior
notes: Implemented TUI visibility hardening: explicit no-session message, non-interactive fallback to report JSON, startup launch banner, and persistent footer help/controls line in TUI.

title: Add plugin token-usage attribution tracker
description:
Summary
Build Sherlock attribution that measures and explains token overhead introduced by plugins, hooks, and MCP/tool paths.

Problem
Token spikes are hard to diagnose without per-source attribution.

Scope
- Capture baseline model token usage per request/turn
- Attribute incremental usage to plugin/hook/tool-triggered actions
- Persist structured logs (session_id, source/plugin identifiers, event, estimated tokens, timestamp)
- Provide summary report of top token consumers
- Add optional guardrail/warning when attributed usage exceeds threshold

Acceptance Criteria
- Reproducible session report with attribution by source
- At least one integration test for synthetic attributed event
- Docs explain setup, caveats, and interpretation

Notes
Prefer non-invasive instrumentation first; maintain CQ/BD compatibility where applicable.
notes:
Migrated from claude-qji in /home/lunaris/build/claude. Sherlock tracking now lives in this repository.
Research-first + algorithmic design first remains required. Adapt existing Sherlock spec/progress notes to this repo paths.
Improved Rust ingest attribution for real Claude session logs: auto-detect latest real sessionId from history, filter ingest to session lines, parse nested message.usage token fields (input/output/cache read/cache creation), classify tool_use + hook subtype sources, and compute meaningful spike windows + source leaderboard in report/TUI from cumulative totals.
Changed ingest default to Claude in-depth session logs first: when --history is omitted, Sherlock now selects latest ~/.claude/projects/<project-key>/*.jsonl for --project-root, then latest project session globally, and only falls back to ~/.claude/history.jsonl.
Improved report interpretability and source attribution: report now includes totals (input/output/cache read/cache write), derived insights, and per-source estimated token contribution. Source grouping now carries plugin_id (e.g., skill:<name>) and MCP server extraction from mcp__ tool names. TUI source table now shows plugin column plus estimated tokens instead of raw event counts.
Expanded plugin/source extraction: now derives tool names from toolUseResult.commandName, tags Skill calls as skill:<name>, tags MCP tool calls as plugin_* or mcp:<server>, and adds tool-result:<command> attribution for tool result events. This improves plugin visibility in report top_sources and TUI source table.
Added explicit plugin_sources section to report so plugin-attributed sources (skill:* / plugin_* / tool-result:*) are visible even when not in top generic sources by token share.
Implemented SQL batching for ingest performance: replaced per-event dolt sql process calls with a single transaction script (START TRANSACTION ... COMMIT) containing batched inserts/updates for sessions/artifacts/sources/turns/events/windows.
Fixed ingest idempotency for repeated runs: session-scoped cleanup now deletes prior turns/events/windows/history artifacts (and dependent attributions) before inserting fresh records, preventing duplicate spikes/sources/totals.

title: Add Claude Code /api/oauth/usage as first-class live-quota source
description:
Anthropic exposes live Claude Code quota data at GET https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage (Bearer token from ~/.claude/.credentials.json, header: anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20). Response includes five_hour, seven_day, per-model sub-limits (seven_day_opus/sonnet/cowork/oauth_apps/omelette), and extra_usage (pay-as-you-go overage). This is the authoritative data Claude Code itself surfaces via /usage — strictly better than JSONL-estimated usage for knowing where the user stands against real rate limits.

Research doc with example payload, credential shape, token-refresh endpoint (https://platform.claude.com/v1/oauth/token), and how endpoints were reverse-engineered from the ELF is committed at docs/claude-code-oauth-usage.md.

Scope:
- New source claude_code_oauth (sidecar or provider).
- Read-only access to ~/.claude/.credentials.json; never log/persist tokens.
- 60s cache. On 401, back off and let Claude Code refresh creds on disk.
- Cross-check OAuth-reported 7d utilization vs. ccusage-style cost totals from the existing claude_code JSONL provider — divergence flags billing surprises.
- Redact tokens from any debug output / agent traces.
close_reason: Shipped in v0.4.0 (commit 41d73c9). Cross-check follow-up filed as sherlock-h4u.

title: investigate https://github.com/lis186/ccxray
notes:
# ccxray investigation

https://github.com/lis186/ccxray — 127★, MIT, JS/Node. Latest v1.2.5 (2026-04-11).

## What it is
Transparent HTTP proxy on :5577 sitting inline between Claude Code and api.anthropic.com. Records every req/res as JSON to ~/.ccxray/logs/, serves a live dashboard on the same port. Hub model: multiple `ccxray claude` invocations share one dashboard.

## Architecture vs sherlock
- ccxray: **live inline proxy**, Claude Code only, JS, real-time dashboard.
- sherlock: **post-hoc log forensics**, multi-provider (claude-code/codex/copilot/antigravity/cursor), Rust, Dolt-backed, LLM narration.

Different shape — sherlock is not going to become a proxy. But several ccxray **display/analysis** features are borrowable since sherlock already reads the same underlying data (Claude Code JSONL carries system prompts, thinking blocks, tool-call content).

## Features worth stealing
1. **System prompt version tracking + diff viewer** — fingerprint per turn, detect version bumps across sessions, show what changed between Claude Code releases. JSONL already carries this.
2. **Per-turn thinking-block duration** — JSONL has thinking content + turn timestamps; derive "how long did the model think".
3. **Subagent taxonomy** — Explore / Web Search / Plan / Plugin agents classified explicitly. Sherlock has `source_kind` already (and sherlock-8xo is about the `core` bucket dominating); ccxray's labels are a more user-facing slice.
4. **Session heatmap + burn-rate graph** — TUI additions on top of existing per-session token totals.

## Not worth copying
- Proxy/hub model (wrong shape for sherlock).
- Multi-project hub auto-detect (n/a for post-hoc).
- Docker image (sherlock is a CLI).

## Follow-up beads filed
- system prompt version tracking
- thinking-block duration metric
- subagent taxonomy enrichment
close_reason: investigation complete; findings in notes; three follow-up features filed (sherlock-egb, sherlock-dqr, sherlock-uwq)

title: rollup --since silently returns 0 when sessions.started_at malformed
description:
When session started_at values are malformed epoch-like strings (e.g. '1776361213Z'), `sherlock rollup --since 2026-04-16 --provider claude-code` returns '0 sessions, 0 total tokens' even though sessions exist in the repo. Removing --since surfaces all 29 sessions correctly.

Same data-quality issue previously flagged in claude-usage-improvement-report.md (2026-04-16) — this tool bug means the report workflow silently undercounts unless the user knows to omit --since and post-filter.

Repro:
1. Ingest histories whose started_at is an epoch-like string ('1776...Z').
2. `sherlock rollup --since 2026-04-16`.
3. Observe empty output despite populated `sessions` table.

Expected: fall back to `windows.end_time` (or events) when sessions.started_at is unparseable, matching the authoritative filter described in the prior workflow. Alternatively, emit a warning instead of silently zeroing.
close_reason: Implemented: new  subcommand + robust timestamp filter (iso_now now emits proper ISO8601; rollup filter tolerates legacy epoch-Z via session_ids_in_window fallback to windows/events).

title: Cross-session plugin rollup report
description: `sherlock report` is per-session. For forge/fleet usage we need an aggregated rollup across a date range or across all ingested sessions: top N plugins by total tokens, event count, and % of spend, optionally filtered by provider. Proposed CLI: `sherlock report --group-by plugin --since 2026-04-01 [--provider claude-code] [--top 20] [--format json|table]`. Drives the ability to answer 'which plugin is burning the most money this month?' without stitching per-session JSON manually. Requested by forge (forge/claude-qji).

title: subagent taxonomy enrichment (Explore/Plan/WebSearch/etc.)
description:
Borrowed from ccxray investigation (sherlock-7br). Related to sherlock-8xo (headline source_kind bucket dominated by 'core').

ccxray labels Claude Code subagents explicitly: Explore, Web Search, Plan, Plugin agents. Sherlock's source_kind already classifies but the 'core' bucket swallows most traffic, hiding which sub-agent actually drove spend.

## Why
Top_sources report is less useful when 'core' is the catch-all. Splitting by subagent_type would let users see 'Explore burned 40%' or 'a plugin agent drove the spike'.

## How to apply
- Detect subagent_type from Agent tool calls in the turn stream (subagent_type param) and tag downstream turns.
- Add subagent_type to the source taxonomy, surface in top_sources.
- Likely fixes or complements sherlock-8xo — cross-reference on close.
close_reason: Implemented in v0.5.0: subagent_type column, sidechain ingestion, headline query now prefers subagent_type and excludes bare core rows

title: per-turn thinking-block duration metric
description:
Borrowed from ccxray investigation (sherlock-7br).

Claude Code JSONL carries thinking-block content + turn start/end timestamps. Derive a 'thinking duration' per turn (approximate: time between the turn request and the first non-thinking token). Aggregate per session and per source_kind to surface 'agent thought for 42s before calling a tool'.

## Why
Latency-to-first-useful-output is an underexposed cost driver. ccxray shows per-turn thinking time prominently; sherlock should expose it in reports too.

## How to apply
- New numeric column on the turn row: thinking_ms.
- Report: p50/p95 thinking time per session + top slowest turns.
- Note: JSONL timestamps may not split thinking vs generation cleanly; start with 'turn wall-clock duration' and refine if the data supports it.

title: system prompt version tracking + diff across sessions
description:
Borrowed from ccxray investigation (sherlock-7br).

Claude Code JSONL carries the full system prompt per turn. Track a fingerprint (sha256 of normalized prompt text) per session, detect when the prompt changes between sessions (= Claude Code release bump or user config change), and surface a diff in the TUI / report output.

## Why
Users can't otherwise see what shifted between a cheap week and an expensive week — often it's a new system-prompt bump pushing more context. ccxray makes this visible; sherlock's post-hoc analysis should too.

## How to apply
- New table (Dolt) keyed by fingerprint → first_seen, last_seen, byte_len, sample_session_id.
- During ingest: hash each distinct system prompt, upsert.
- Report: "system prompt versions seen in this window" + unified diff between adjacent versions.
- TUI: drill-down view.

title: Cross-check OAuth 7d utilization vs ccusage JSONL totals
description:
Scope carved out of sherlock-enl (closed with v0.4.0). OAuth live quota and transcript-derived ccusage estimates both exist now; wire them side-by-side so wide divergence flags billing surprises.

Goals:
- Extend `sherlock quota` (or a new `sherlock reconcile`) to fetch OAuth `seven_day.utilization` and compute a rough 7d cost estimate from the existing claude_code JSONL provider.
- Render both numbers plus delta; flag > N% absolute divergence as a finding.
- Keep OAuth source authoritative for rate-limit state — divergence is a signal about cost accounting, not limits.

Out of scope:
- Refreshing OAuth tokens (user re-runs `claude` when 401 hits, per docs/claude-code-oauth-usage.md open item).

title: headline top_sources dominated by source_kind='core' bucket
description:
Sherlock's Claude Code ingest tags most assistant events with source_kind='core' (empty plugin/tool), so the `headline` report's top-sources bucket is almost always {key: 'core', event_count: <huge>}. Real tool/plugin names are drowned out.

Repro: `sherlock headline --roots ~/build --modified-since 7d`. Top source per repo is invariably "core".

Fix options:
- Exclude source_kind='core' from headline top-sources query (most useful).
- Or weight by estimated tokens (cumulative-diff) instead of event_count so "core" no-op events count for less.
- Or break out "core" into its own aggregate line and show meaningful tools separately.

Scope: low-impact UX polish; feature works, data is correct.
close_reason: Implemented in v0.5.0: subagent_type column, sidechain ingestion, headline query now prefers subagent_type and excludes bare core rows

title: dolt repo fails on read-only sandbox filesystems — need user-writable default
description:
Default repo at /home/lunaris/.local/share/sherlock is not always writable from sandboxed agent contexts (Claude Code strict sandbox allows writes only inside \$TMPDIR and cwd). Dolt errors with 'read-only file system' for every subcommand (ingest, rollup, list-aliases, etc.).

Workaround today: `--repo \$TMPDIR/sherlock` + re-init + re-ingest per session — expensive, defeats persistence.

Would prefer:
- Auto-detect write perms on default repo; if unwritable, emit a clear error with fix (e.g. 'pass --repo <writable-path>').
- Or: respect \$SHERLOCK_REPO env var as default override so users can once-set it in shellrc and never pass --repo again.
- Or: lazily fall back to \$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/sherlock read-only mirror when the primary is write-locked.

title: Threshold-based plugin spend warnings
description: Sherlock is forensics-only; it has no guardrail surface. Add an opt-in warning pass that flags when any single plugin exceeds a configurable % of session spend or absolute token count, emitted as structured output (JSON + non-zero exit or printed WARN lines). Proposed CLI: `sherlock report --warn-plugin-share 0.25 --warn-plugin-tokens 50000 --exit-code-on-warn`. Enables forge daemon / CI checks to auto-flag regressions introduced by new plugins. Keeps active-blocking out of scope — this is post-hoc signal only. Requested by forge (forge/claude-qji).

value: Sherlock's issue with beads: Sherlock uses dolt CLI commands (dolt sql, dolt commit) which can lock/interfere with running dolt sql-server instances. The fix is to ensure Sherlock users are aware of running dolt servers before executing commands. Long-term solution would be to use dolt SQL server protocol instead of CLI.
